first-brick.title: Your first brick
intro: Every brick is an empty `<div>`. With nothing inside, it has no size at all. `padding` adds space inside the brick, and that space is what you see.
`padding: 10px` adds 10px on every side, so the brick becomes 20px × 20px: exactly one stud.
first-brick.goal: Make the brick 2 studs wide and 2 studs tall (40px × 40px).
hints: Padding is added on both sides: left + right gives the width, top + bottom gives the height.
You need 40px in total, so each side needs half of that.
Change the value to `padding: 20px;`
first-brick.recap: `padding` grows a brick from the inside. Half the size you want goes on each side.

long-brick.title: A long brick
intro: `padding` can take two values: the first one is for top and bottom, the second one is for left and right.
That is how you get long bricks instead of squares.
long-brick.goal: Make a brick 4 studs wide and 2 studs tall (80px × 40px).
hints: The height stays 40px, so top and bottom stay at 20px each.
The width must be 80px: that is 40px on the left and 40px on the right.
Write `padding: 20px 40px;`
long-brick.recap: With two values, `padding: vertical horizontal;` lets you shape the brick.

standing-brick.title: Turn it around
intro: Swap the two values and the brick turns around: a big first value makes it tall, a big second value makes it wide.
standing-brick.goal: Make a brick 1 stud wide and 4 studs tall (20px × 80px).
hints: Tall means a big first value (top and bottom).
Height 80px → 40px top and bottom. Width 20px → 10px left and right.
Write `padding: 40px 10px;`
standing-brick.recap: The first value controls the height, the second one the width.

two-sizes.title: Two bricks, two sizes
intro: A brick can have several classes. `class="brick small"` means the brick gets the rules of `.brick` and the rules of `.small`.
Rules in `.brick` apply to every brick. Rules in `.small` or `.large` only apply to that brick, and they win over `.brick` because they come later in the file.
two-sizes.goal: Make the small brick 2 × 2 studs and the large brick 6 studs wide and 4 studs tall.
hints: Write the padding inside `.small { }` and `.large { }`, not in `.brick`.
Small: 40px × 40px. Large: 120px wide, 80px tall.
`.small { padding: 20px; }` and `.large { padding: 40px 60px; }`
two-sizes.recap: Shared rules go on `.brick`; each extra class adds what is special about one brick.

paint-it.title: Paint it red
intro: Bricks start out unpainted. `background-color` paints the inside of the brick, padding included.
CSS knows color names like `red`, `yellow`, `blue`, `green`, `orange`, `purple`, `white` and `black`.
hints: Add a new line inside `.brick { }`. Every line is `property: value;`
Write `background-color: red;` under the padding.
paint-it.recap: `background-color` paints the brick. Don't forget the `;` at the end of each line.

three-colors.title: Three colors
intro: All three bricks share the `.brick` rules, so they have the same size. Their second class lets you paint each one differently.
three-colors.goal: Paint the bricks red, yellow and blue, from left to right.
hints: `.one` is already done. Copy its line into `.two` and `.three`.
Change the color name: `yellow` for `.two`, `blue` for `.three`.
three-colors.recap: One class for what bricks share, one class for what makes each brick different.

brick-sorter.title: Brick sorter
intro: Now size and color together. Each brick needs its own `padding` and its own `background-color`.
Look at the dashed outlines in the preview: they show where each brick must end up and which color it needs.
brick-sorter.goal: A green 2 × 2 square, an orange brick 6 studs wide and 2 tall, and a purple post 1 stud wide and 5 tall.
hints: Each stud is 20px. Divide the size you want by 2 to get the padding of one side.
Square: `padding: 20px;` Long: `padding: 20px 60px;` Post: `padding: 50px 10px;`
Then add `background-color: green;`, `orange` and `purple`.
brick-sorter.recap: Size with `padding`, color with `background-color`: you can now make any brick.

move-right.title: Move it right
intro: `padding` is space inside the brick. `margin` is space outside it: it pushes the brick away from what is around it.
`margin-left: 40px` leaves 40px empty on the left of the brick, so it moves 2 studs to the right.
move-right.goal: Move the red brick 6 studs to the right.
hints: You need empty space on the left of the brick: `margin-left`.
6 studs × 20px = 120px.
Add `margin-left: 120px;`
move-right.recap: `margin` is invisible space outside a brick. It moves the brick without changing its size.

move-down.title: Down and across
intro: `margin-top` pushes a brick down. Combine it with `margin-left` to place a brick anywhere on the baseplate.
There is also a short form with four values, clockwise from the top: `margin: top right bottom left;`
move-down.goal: Place the brick 10 studs from the left and 4 studs from the top.
hints: Two margins: one from the left, one from the top.
10 studs = 200px from the left, 4 studs = 80px from the top.
`margin-left: 200px;` and `margin-top: 80px;` (or `margin: 80px 0 0 200px;`)
move-down.recap: `margin-top` and `margin-left` place a brick at an exact spot.

staircase.title: Staircase
intro: Margins of one brick also push its neighbours. `margin-right` on every brick leaves a gap after each one.
Give each step its own `margin-top` to move it lower than the one before.
staircase.goal: Build a staircase: one stud between the steps, each step 2 studs lower than the previous one.
hints: The space between steps is the same for all of them: put `margin-right: 20px;` in `.brick`.
The first step stays at the top. The second goes 2 studs down, the third 4 studs down.
`.two { margin-top: 40px; }` and `.three { margin-top: 80px; }`
staircase.recap: A margin pushes neighbours too. Shared spacing goes on `.brick`, special offsets on each step.

center-stage.title: Center stage
intro: Counting margins gets tiring. The baseplate is a flex container (`display: flex`): it lines up the bricks inside it in a row, and it can place them for you.
`justify-content` moves the bricks along the row: `flex-start` (left, the default), `center`, `flex-end` (right).
This rule goes on the container, `.baseplate`, not on the bricks.
center-stage.goal: Center the yellow brick horizontally, without using margin.
hints: Write the new line inside `.baseplate { }`.
Add `justify-content: center;`
center-stage.recap: `justify-content` on the container places all its bricks along the row.

push-right.title: Push to the end
intro: `justify-content: flex-end` pushes all the bricks to the end of the row, keeping their order.
push-right.goal: Move the three bricks to the right edge of the baseplate.
hints: The end of a row is its right side.
Add `justify-content: flex-end;` to `.baseplate`.
push-right.recap: `flex-end` packs the bricks at the end of the row.

spread-out.title: Spread out
intro: `justify-content: space-between` puts the first brick at the start, the last one at the end, and shares the free space equally between them.
Other options: `space-around` and `space-evenly` also put space at the edges.
spread-out.goal: Spread the four bricks across the full width of the baseplate.
hints: The first brick touches the left edge, the last one the right edge.
Use `justify-content: space-between;`
spread-out.recap: `space-between` spreads bricks with equal space between them.

dead-center.title: Dead center
intro: `justify-content` works along the row (horizontal). `align-items` works across it (vertical): `flex-start` (top), `center`, `flex-end` (bottom).
Together they can put a brick right in the middle of the baseplate.
dead-center.goal: Put the brick in the exact center of the baseplate.
hints: It is already centered from left to right. Now center it from top to bottom.
Add `align-items: center;` to `.baseplate`.
dead-center.recap: In a row: `justify-content` is horizontal, `align-items` is vertical.

traffic-light.title: Traffic light
intro: `flex-direction` chooses how bricks line up: `row` (side by side, the default) or `column` (stacked from top to bottom).
traffic-light.goal: Stack the bricks into a traffic light: red on top, then yellow, then green.
hints: The bricks are in a row. You want a column.
Add `flex-direction: column;` to `.baseplate`.
traffic-light.recap: `flex-direction: column` stacks bricks from top to bottom.

axis-swap.title: The axes swap
intro: In a column, the two properties swap roles: `justify-content` now moves bricks up and down, and `align-items` moves them left and right.
Rule of thumb: `justify-content` follows the direction of the line, `align-items` goes across it.
axis-swap.goal: Move the traffic light to the right edge, centered from top to bottom.
hints: Centered from top to bottom, in a column: that is `justify-content`.
Pushed to the right edge, in a column: that is `align-items`.
`justify-content: center;` and `align-items: flex-end;`
axis-swap.recap: Change the direction and the two axes swap: always ask "along the line or across it?".

mind-the-gap.title: Mind the gap
intro: `gap` on a flex container adds the same space between every pair of bricks, but not before the first one or after the last one.
It is simpler than adding margins to each brick, and the bricks stay centered.
mind-the-gap.goal: Leave 2 studs between the four centered bricks.
hints: `gap` goes on the container, `.baseplate`.
2 studs = 40px. Add `gap: 40px;`
mind-the-gap.recap: `gap` spaces bricks evenly without touching their margins.

pyramid.title: Pyramid
intro: Time to combine everything you know about flex: direction, both alignments and gap.
Each brick already has its size and color. Only `.baseplate` needs work.
pyramid.goal: Build a pyramid at the bottom of the baseplate, centered, with 1 stud between the layers.
hints: The layers are stacked: start with `flex-direction: column;`
In a column, "at the bottom" is `justify-content` and "centered left to right" is `align-items`.
`justify-content: flex-end;`, `align-items: center;` and `gap: 20px;`
pyramid.recap: Direction, alignment on both axes and gap: that is the whole flex toolbox.

add-a-brick.title: Add a brick
intro:
Until now the HTML was fixed. In this step you write it. Open the HTML tab: each brick is one element, `
`.

An element has an opening tag `
` and a closing tag `
`. The `class` attribute lists the classes the CSS can target.
add-a-brick.goal: Add a blue brick after the yellow one. The CSS is ready.
hints: Copy the yellow brick's line and paste it below.
Change `yellow` to `blue` in the class.

Add `
` on a new line at the end.
add-a-brick.recap: HTML says what is there, CSS says how it looks. One `<div>` = one brick.

house.title: Build a house
intro: A `<div>` can hold other elements. The `.row` div holds the walls and the door, and it can line them up on its own, but only once you give it `display: flex`.
The baseplate stacks the roof and the row. The row puts its bricks side by side. Every container has its own `flex-direction`, `justify-content`, `align-items` and `gap`.
This is the final build: you need everything from the previous 19 steps.
house.goal: Add the second wall in the HTML, then style the house: a red roof on top of white walls with a blue door, centered on the baseplate.
hints:
HTML first: inside `.row`, add `
` after the door.
Bricks: roof `padding: 20px 80px;`, wall `padding: 40px 20px;`, door `padding: 30px 20px;`, each with its color.
`.baseplate`: `flex-direction: column;` with `justify-content: center;` and `align-items: center;`
`.row`: `display: flex;`, `align-items: flex-end;` and `gap: 20px;`
house.recap: Containers inside containers: that is how every real web page is laid out. Well built!
